text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- The postal service, Posten Norge, which manages more than 50 billion crowns for businesses and citizens, must take criticism from the state's General Auditing Office for bad handling of its accounts, taxes and charges for 1996. The auditors are questioning whether the large state company has given in the correct information.

- The number of people on hospital waiting lists has declined for the first time. At the end of April, 16,332 listed patients had waited more than six months for treatment compared with 19,457 at the end of 1996.

- The Finance Ministry will likely answer to a complaint from Aker RGI over a recommendation by the Norwegian Banking, Insurance and Securities Commission on its shareholding in insurer Storebrand before Storebrand's annual general meeting next Thursday. The commission recommended that Aker RGI's shareholding in Storeband be combined with three other major shareholders into one stake.

- A big quarrel is brewing between Statoil and Norsk Hydro over who will treat wet gas from the Oseberg field in the North Sea, which is due to begin production in 1999. Norsk Hydro wants to invest one billion crowns in a gas treatment plant at Sture, north of Bergen on the west coast. Statoil wants to spend 1.5 billion crowns on a similar plant near its Mongstad refinery.

- Den norske Bank (DnB) and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse have most to gain from a merger with other large Nordic banks, according to a new study by the Foundation for Research in Economics and Business Administration (SNF). SNF says among other things a fusion between a large Norwegian bank and a large Danish or Swedish bank would strengthen the merged institution in terms of international payment transactions.

- Repant AS, a small producer of return bottle and can machines, is taking up the competition battle with market giant Tomra ASA. Repant plans to invest 10 million crowns in fresh capital and to reach a turnover of at least 30 million crowns in the next two years.
